title: A play is admitted only when the workers with room keep it at real time, alone or together; one they cannot keep is refused within seconds with its reason
description: JS-154: the dogfood's 4-core i5-6500 needs 3.8 to 4.1 CPU-seconds per second of a 4K HDR re-encode priced at 3.2, a figure measured on a machine 1.6 times faster per core; the job is admitted, runs at 0.85x and stalls with no reason. Prices stay one table in cores of a named reference machine; each worker measures its own speed against it at start and advertises its capacity in those units. D-044. D-046: a play that no one worker holds but the workers with room hold together is admitted, and a viewer already watching is never taken under real time by a newcomer.
acceptanceCriteria: Design reviewed before building: how capacity reaches every replica, a rolling upgrade beside workers of the release before, and whether an image-track extraction counts against capacity. Amended by D-046: the rule for a play no one worker holds but several hold together, stated with its margin from a measurement and not from adding speeds; what a play admitted that way holds (its helpers) against a new viewer; and whether the task is too large for one build. If it is, it splits there into (a) worker speed, single-worker admission and placement and (b) shared admission, in that order, both ahead of JS-166, and (a) alone never refuses a play that two workers with room would hold together. Amended by D-050: the review also says what a queued viewer job that fits no worker holds back, whether paused helpers keep cores a newcomer could use (BL-008), and whether the insert and the claim judging room by different ledgers can admit a play that is never claimed or refuse one that fits; each "yes" gets a check or comes back as a brief. Amended by D-051: the review says whether a play admitted as shared gets its helpers at its start and at a seek, from JS-174's figures if they are in; if they are not, the task does not wait, criterion 3's bound stands, and a miss comes back as a brief. Amended by D-062: no measurement at start; the review says how an undeclared worker's assumed capacity reaches every replica.

A worker that declares nothing counts each of its processors at the reference machine's speed, registers at once, and runs no benchmark at start or beside its work, declared or not. Its log at start and /metrics give the capacity it counts and whether it was declared or assumed; /metrics shows as capacity only what admission counts. transcodeCores overrides it. docs/running.md says a CPU slower than the reference, or SMT threads, make an undeclared worker overstate itself, what a viewer then sees, and how to choose transcodeCores from docs/transcoding.md's figures. `jellyscale_transcode_worker_speed` and `jellyscale_transcode_speed_measurement_failures_total` leave /metrics and the docs. (D-062)

With real processes: a worker throttled to the i5-6500's speed and declaring its computed capacity, alone, refuses a 4K HDR tone mapped re-encode within seconds with the 'cannot be played at this time' dialog in jellyfin-web; the log and the JS-153 decision line give the reason with the job's cost and the worker's capacity; the same play beside a second worker that holds it is made by that worker. Amended by D-046: the same play beside a second worker throttled to the same speed, helpers on, is admitted and plays in jellyfin-web for 10 minutes, a seek to the middle and 10 minutes more within JS-168's bound (speed at or above 1.0 after each part's first 30 seconds, no more than 3 freezes of 0.5 seconds or more per 10 minutes, none over 2 seconds); with transcodeHelpers off, or with the second worker's cores taken, it is refused within seconds with its reason. (D-062: the throttled workers declare the i5-6500's computed figure.)
A worker at the reference machine's speed holds exactly the jobs it holds today; every row of the table is admitted by the same rule, not only the 4K one
A worker given jobs that add up to its declared capacity keeps each at 1.2 times real time or more without a helper

A default worker is no longer floored to the dearest job; one that cannot hold the dearest row says so once at start, in the log and on /metrics; listed under Changed guarantees citing D-044 Judged on the counted capacity (D-044, D-062).

A running re-encode under 1.2 times real time that gets no helper logs once why, and the reason is counted on /metrics (BL-005) On a worker that declared nothing the line says its capacity is assumed and names transcodeCores, and the counted reason tells assumed from declared (D-062).
docs/transcoding.md names the reference machine and gives the i5-6500 figures; docs/status.md's gap line is updated

With workers of unequal speed, a job is given to a worker that can hold it at real time when one has room: with one free worker that holds the job at 1.2 times real time alone and one free worker that does not, the viewer's job goes to the one that holds it in 10 of 10 plays from the start and 10 of 10 after a seek, with real processes (JS-162: it landed on the small worker in 2 of 2 natural first plays and stalled) (D-045; made exact by D-046)
the decision line (JS-153) and the log say whether a play was admitted on one worker or shared, with the job's cost and the capacities counted.

A viewer already watching at real time is never taken under it by another viewer starting (D-046, confirmed by D-050: in JS-168's measurement a newcomer who stopped the helper took the first viewer from 1.00x to 0.68–0.82x with 44 to 54 freezes in 5 minutes, 6 runs of 6, and started no sooner than on an idle cluster). One figure decides it, the 1.2 times real time admission already uses: a helper of a watched job that its own worker does not hold at 1.2 alone is held as that play's own, and a new viewer whose job fits only by stopping such a helper is refused within seconds with its reason, whatever the newcomer's job costs. A helper of a job its worker holds at 1.2 alone is still stopped for a new viewer, as today. A viewer who joins a re-encode already running (same film, same output) starts no new job and is never refused by this rule. No helper is stopped, delayed or left unclaimed for a newcomer who is then not admitted: a refused play, or a queued viewer job no worker can fit, holds back only a helper that would take cores that job could use (takes BL-014 and JS-168's viewer-first-gate finding). The refusal's reason says the cores are held by a film another viewer is watching, apart from "no free cores", in the log, the JS-153 decision line and the counted reason JS-164 reads as demand; no label names a job, film, account or device. Locked check, real processes, two throttled workers and a fixture film: with a helper the first job needs running, a second play of the same cost and a 1080p SDR one are each refused within 5 seconds, the helper is not stopped and the first job's speed does not fall below 1.0; when the first viewer stops, the same second play is admitted. Recorded measurement on the build, not a locked check, taken by the lead beside the next task (D-061: one run of each kind of second play): two real workers and two viewers in jellyfin-web; the second viewer sees the "cannot be played at this time" dialog, and the first viewer's speed stays at or above 1.0 with no freeze over 2 seconds and no more than 2 freezes of 0.5 seconds or more in the 5 minutes after the second asks. docs/running.md (the transcodeHelpers paragraph, which says a new viewer stops helpers) and DOMAINS.md invariant 58 are amended, and docs/running.md says what this refusal means and that room for one more film, kept by sizing or the autoscaler, avoids it. Listed under Changed guarantees citing D-046 and D-050 (today a new viewer stops any helper).

test/roles.sh's restart check, the e2e stack and the differential stack run with workers that declare nothing, as before JS-161; any declaration kept is named with the check that needs it. The 9 cmd/jellyscale tests of run 45135324010 pass unamended, except assertions on the measurement itself, in a 4-process run on 4 pinned CPUs; one that still fails returns as a brief. The two checks that guard a request waiting through a restart and a job claimed within the queue window are not touched. (D-062)
notes: The measured 3.8 to 4.1 straddles the dogfood's 4 cores: the criteria are outcomes, not a raised number. It merges when ready. If the dogfood would then refuse plays it stalls on today, the lead tells the owner before the redeploy that carries it (the owner declined that outcome by config on 2026-11-21; D-045). on a cluster one shared film fills, a second viewer is refused with a reason, even for a cheap film, where today they would start. Today the first viewer stalls in that cluster whether or not a second arrives. Refusal with a reason is the floor D-044 set; a silent stall for someone who was watching is not offered. Data that reopens it: the dogfood's count of refusals made while a helper held the cores, against the first viewers' stalls it prevented, from JS-153's counters and JS-164's gauge. (D-046) D-050 confirmed the default on JS-168's figures. Data that reopens it: the dogfood's count of refusals with the helper-held reason against the first viewers' stalls prevented, or the measurement held in the backlog (a cheap play beside the helper). Before this task's Spec, the second-viewer figures are in docs/transcoding.md on main with machine and command (D-050). Done 2026-11-23 (#258), without a start-up measurement (D-062).
